meta.idea: A marketplace where people list things they no longer want, chat with a buyer, and agree on a sale.

stack.name: Next.js + SQLite
stack.why: One project runs both the screens and the server, and the database is a single file you can delete and start over.

roles.summary: Decides how the app is put together and what the data looks like, before anyone writes a feature.
responsibilities: Decide what a listing, a user, and a chat message look like as data
Write down the folder layout the rest of the team will build into
Write down the addresses (API routes) the screens will call

roles.summary: Builds the screens people actually click on.
responsibilities: Build the listing feed, the listing detail page, and the upload form
Handle loading and empty states so the app never looks broken

roles.summary: Builds login, the database, and everything that happens behind the screens.
responsibilities: Create the database tables for users, listings, and messages
Build sign up and log in
Build the API routes the screens call

roles.summary: Checks the others' work for bugs and missing pieces before you call it done.
responsibilities: Walk through the whole flow: sign up, post a listing, message the seller
Write tests for the parts most likely to break
Report anything the other agents left half-finished

ownership.note: Both sides use this file. Add to it, never rewrite what is already there, and say what you added when you finish.
Both sides use this file. Add to it, never rewrite what is already there, and say what you added when you finish.

steps.title: Plan the structure
steps.goal: Decide the shape of the data and the folder layout so the other two never have to guess.
tasks: Write docs/architecture.md describing the folders and what goes in each
Write docs/data-model.md describing users, listings, and messages and how they relate
Write docs/api.md listing every address the screens will call, with what goes in and what comes back
Create shared/types.ts with the TypeScript types for users, listings, and messages
doneWhen: docs/architecture.md, docs/data-model.md and docs/api.md all exist
shared/types.ts exists and lists a type for users, listings and messages
No code outside docs/ and shared/types.ts was created

steps.title: Build the database and login
steps.goal: Make the server side real: tables, accounts, and the addresses the screens will call.
tasks: Read docs/data-model.md and docs/api.md first
Create the database tables described there
Build sign up and log in
Build every API route listed in docs/api.md
Confirm each route returns the shape docs/api.md promises
doneWhen: The database file is created when the app starts
A new account can be created and logged into
Every route in docs/api.md exists and returns real data

steps.title: Build the screens
steps.goal: Build every screen a user touches, using the addresses the Architect wrote down.
tasks: Read docs/api.md first so the screens call the right addresses
Build the listing feed and the listing detail page
Build the upload form for posting an item
Build the chat screen
Show something sensible while loading and when there is nothing to show
doneWhen: Every screen can be reached by clicking, with no dead links
The feed shows listings that came from the server, not fake placeholder data
Nothing in server/ or db/ was changed

steps.title: Check the whole thing
steps.goal: Find what is broken or missing before the owner calls this finished.
tasks: Run the app and go through it as a real user: sign up, post an item, message the seller
Write tests for sign up, posting a listing, and sending a message
List anything half-finished, and say which teammate should fix it
doneWhen: Tests exist for sign up, posting a listing, and sending a message
A written list of remaining problems exists, each one assigned to a teammate

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.goal: Open what your team built and use it the way a stranger would.
tasks: Start the app the way the README says
Sign up as a new person and post something for sale
Open a second browser window, sign up as someone else, and message the seller
Try something silly on purpose: an empty title, a very long description
Write down anything that looked wrong or confusing
doneWhen: The app opens without an error
You posted a listing and saw it appear in the feed
A message you sent as one person showed up for the other
You have a written list of anything that looked wrong
